newsitem.title: USA: CSCE March coffee sets new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE March coffee sets new contract highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures renewed their push upward ahead of midday, setting fresh contract highs as a round of speculative buying broke the market through key resistance levels, traders said.
At 1124 EST, March delivery rose 5.65 cents a lb, to 177.50 cents, the new contract scored after key resistance was pierced at 177.00.
The low was 174.00 cents. Second-month May was up 3.80 cents, to 167.00 cents, while the rest were 0.30 to 3.25 cents higher.

Prices gapped higher from the opening, hitting new contract highs, but speculators, led by commission houses, moved to take profit after the spot March contract initially failed to breach key resistance at 177.00 cents per lb.
"It seemed like momentary resistance triggered some profit taking," one broker said. "But at any breaks you see the buying coming back in."

Although a strike by Colombian state workers should not have a major impact on that country's coffee trade, dealers said concerns the work stoppage may delay exports continued to fuel bullish sentiment.
"The strike should not really affect coffee, but there is such uncertainty it creates nervousness because of the already tight situation," one trader said.
Labor leaders renewed talks with government officials early Thursday in a bid to end the work stoppage, which entered its third day and is being billed as the biggest in 20 years.
Traders are also closely monitoring the March/May spread, a barometer of nearby availability. The spread continued to widen from Wednesday's close at 9.55 cents.
But with first notice day for CSCE March coffee next Thursday and more than 16,000 contracts of open interest remaining in March, traders said the spread could push out further.
Volume as of 1100 EST, reached an estimated 5,880 lots.
